deviation: Device table: the machine has a 16 GB RTX 2000 Ada (not the planned 20 GB A4500), so the model runs exp17's FP8 W8A8 path (load_model(fp8=True)), the same engine as the screen. The engine check therefore tests engine reproduction (REPRODUCED, 100% per-slot agreement), not an FP8-vs-bf16 gap.
HF_HOME was not set to ./hf_cache (the run's shared cache is mandatory; the model lives there, nothing heavy in this folder).

max_new = 1024 for every task including T1/T2 (the screen's and the reused rows' cap; plan: 1,536 for path tasks). The fence stop ends rows at the first closed python block, so the cap binds only for runaway rows.
MINP_T1.6 runs as a 10-row batch (its plan partner 'spare' was empty); it is a sensitivity arm and needs no bit-exact coupling with TWIN.
Unjudged labeller disagreements keep the runtime label (labeller_source='runtime_unjudged'), as plan 5.2 specifies; exp17 marked them 'disputed'.

Disagreement judges: exp11's frozen j1 google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite (bench) and exp8's openai/gpt-4.1-mini (path), as in iteration 3. Label-validity audit: openai/gpt-4.1-mini (bench, frozen exp11 prompt as judge j2) and google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite (path, exp8 suite prompt), i.e. a different model from each family's disagreement judge.

Amendment after commit1 (speed only): src/analysis/hull.py pop_hill vectorised (bit-identical to the committed loop on 500 random compositions, max |diff| = 0) and, inside bootstrap replicates only (refine=False), the P15/P20 crossing between grid neighbours is linearly interpolated instead of bisected. Point estimates and every H5 are unchanged. The committed version is reconstructed at predictions/amendments/hull_commit1_reconstructed.py (sha256 matches commitments.log).

Orchestration and reporting code written after commit1 (src/analysis/run_all.py, descriptive.py, metrics_exp6.py, src/audit_llm.py, figures.py, outputs.py, audit/rederive.py) is chained as commit2. run_all.py was smoke-tested on partial data (T03 complete, T2 template W1) before the full run, which printed an interim C1 verdict on that partial data; the committed decision code (core.c1_decide) and the rule file were not changed afterwards.

Hull unit test: the edge-restricted search matched full-simplex SLSQP within 0.02 on the plan's cases (a)-(d) but NOT on random 5-vertex Dirichlet(0.5) cases (gap 0.19): a 3-vertex mixture can beat every edge. The pre-registered edge search stays primary; a 3-vertex-face grid check is reported per class (results/prices.json triangle_minus_edge).

T1 has no iteration-3 twin among the reused rows (exp16's path screen has none for T1), so the T1 veto classes are priced against this artifact's TWIN (engine mismatch flagged); T2 vetoes use exp16's own twin arm 'b' (20 rows).

Screen reconciliation: T03 counts 8/18 directions at alpha 1 because exp13's rand1-3 (against its HF twin) are pooled with exp17's 15; exp17 alone matches the quoted 7/15 pattern. Reported, not acted on.

Amendment (reproducibility bug fix, before the final analysis): src/analysis/core.py run_bootstrap derived per-task replicate seeds from Python's hash(str), which is salted per process; replaced by zlib.crc32(task) so every bootstrap is reproducible. Statistics unchanged; the committed file is kept at predictions/amendments/core_commit1.py.

Post-hoc finding (labelled): 284 of 350 verbalized-sampling (VS) programs embed a run-time random dispatcher (random.choices over several catalogue algorithms inside solve()); their mechanism label is the branch the labeller's runtime trace hit, so VS 'diversity' is partly a measurement artifact. results/vs_dispatch.json counts them per task; a labelled post-hoc sensitivity s2b (min-p added to NA, VS not) is reported beside the pre-registered s2.

Operational: the GPU stage was restarted twice before the first Stage-1 row: (1) RLIMIT_AS (the RAM cap of the aii-use-hardware skill) made CUDA initialisation fail, so the GPU process runs without it (cgroup limit 28 GB; peak host RAM ~17 GB during FP8 quantisation); (2) decoding was ~6x slower than exp17 because len(tokenizer) (~30 ms) was evaluated once per generated token while decoding text; it is now cached. Finished steps (unit tests, R2 unit, engine-check rows) resumed from their files; no sample row was generated twice or changed.

The time rule at stage 100 (extrapolation only) kept every arm and N = 50 (5 templates x 10 slots) on all 15 tasks, P3 included; the full queue finished at 07:34 UTC with no not-run cell (results/queue_result.json).
Label-validity audit: on T06 and T10 the best NA knob is the reused iterated veto, so its sampled programs come from the exp13 reused rows (vLLM bf16 engine).
